speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they are triggered by touching the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myringo-osteoma formation (osteoid hyperplasia of the tympanic remnant).
I have identified your history of recurrent infections and the specific timing of pain during chewing and earring wear, which strongly suggests bone growth rather than simple granulation. Given your age and the 12-week post-op timeline, this is consistent with osteoid tissue overgrowing the tympanic remnant. Do you notice any changes in your hearing or a feeling of fullness in the affected ear?
